lesson.subject: literacy
lesson.title: The Big Finish
lesson.subtitle: Term 4 Week 8, Session 5
lesson.footer: Persuasive Speeches | Year 5/6 Literacy | Week 8 Session 5

plan.curriculum: English 2.0, Level 5: VC2E5LY10 creating spoken persuasive texts; VC2E5LY02 planning delivery with notes; VC2E5LA07 cohesive endings that link back
plan.shape: model, guide, apply: the teacher finishes the shade-trees speech and shrinks it to cue cards, students practise endings and key words, then finish, time and card their own speech
plan.criticalFeature: cue cards hold key words, not sentences: three or four words that jog the memory
decisionPoints: the choice check: the best cue card
the exit board: key words for a new sentence
plan.anchor: Claim it. Prove it. Sell it. Say it. Today: Say it, finish strong, and card it.
plan.catchUp: Students with an unfinished middle write a two-line conclusion, then card what they have.

studentTools: S3 opening and S4 middle (in the speech folder)
Five index cards or paper strips per student
routineIcons: Write it, chin it, show me
Point to A, B or C
boardSetup: The finish: restate, echo the hook, call to action
Cue cards: key words only, one card per part

resources.label: Worksheet
resources.description: Your turn: name the parts of a finish, strengthen endings, shrink sentences to key words, then finish and card your speech.
resources.title: The Big Finish
resources.subtitle: Finish strong. Card it. Time it.

example.prompt: So, our school needs ten shade trees.

items.prompt: Next summer, touch the slide. No ouch.

example.prompt: That's the end of my speech. Thank you.
example.answer: So walk with us on Wednesday. Your feet. Our planet.

items.prompt: Rewrite each fizzling ending as a mic-drop call to action.
rows: I hope you liked my speech about plastic.
answers: So yeah, that's my speech.
So join us. Today. Not tomorrow.
I hope you liked my speech about plastic.
Pack a nude-food lunch tomorrow. The ocean is counting on you.
Um, anyway, bears are cool.
Switch off one light tonight. Do it for the bears.

example.prompt: Put your hand on the slide at lunch. Ouch!

items.prompt: Shrink each sentence to cue-card key words.
rows: In February our yard hit 41 degrees.
Shade cuts UV by up to 75 per cent.
Last summer, Sam waited for pickup in the sun.
answers: In February our yard hit 41 degrees.
FEB - 41 DEGREES
Shade cuts UV by up to 75 per cent.
Last summer, Sam waited for pickup in the sun.
SAM - PICKUP - SUN

items.prompt: Tom's cue card has a problem. Find it and fix it.
work: Card 1: Imagine waking up and there are no birds singing at all, not one, because the trees are gone and the birds have nowhere to live.
items.answer: It's a full paragraph; he'll read it, not say it. Fix: NO BIRDS - TREES GONE - NOWHERE

example.answer: So, ten trees. Next summer, touch the slide: no ouch. Say yes on Tuesday.

items.prompt: Write your conclusion: restate, echo your hook, call to action.
items.answer: A restated position, a hook echo and one clear action.

resources.label: Extension
resources.description: Early finisher option: mark pauses and stress on your speech, then plan your answer to a tough question.
resources.title: Speech Coach
resources.subtitle: Mark it up like a pro.

example.prompt: Put your hand on the slide. / Go on. / OUCH.
example.answer: Put your HAND on the slide. / Go on. / OUCH.

items.prompt: Mark pauses (/) and stress (CAPITALS) on each line.
rows: Not next year. Not next week. Today.
One tree would have stopped that.
So I'm asking you: will you help?
answers: Not next year. Not next week. Today.
NOT next year. / NOT next week. / TODAY.
One tree would have stopped that.
ONE tree / would have STOPPED that.
So I'm asking you: will you help?
So I'm asking YOU: / will you HELP?

example.prompt: Question: who will water the trees?
example.answer: Great question. The garden club offered. So: ten trees, yes?

items.prompt: Write the toughest question your audience might ask, and your answer.
items.answer: A realistic question and a short answer that returns to the action.

example.answer: So, we need trees. Please plant ten before summer. Thank you.

items.answer: A restated position and one action.
items.hint: Use your Do from your plan.

slides.notes: Open S5. One line: today the speech gets finished, timed and onto cue cards.
Print the Worksheet for everyone, the Extension for early finishers and the Supported Worksheet for those who need it. Five index cards or paper strips per student; a timer per pair.

slides.learningIntention: We are learning to finish a speech strongly and prepare cue cards to deliver it.
successCriteria: I can name restate, echo the hook and call to action.
I can write a strong finish and shrink my speech to key-word cue cards.
I can mark my speech for pauses and stress.

beats: POINT to the learning intention.
SAY: The last words they hear decide what they do.
SAY: Read the I can lines with me. Everyone, together, on three.
SAY: The first one is where we all start.
The second one is today's main goal.
notes.prep: SC1 is reachable for all; SC2 is the core and the exit evidence; SC3 is the stretch.

slides.title: Read it, or say it?
lines: Watch me give my opening twice.
Once reading a full page. Once with one small card.

notes.answer: the cue card version - eye contact and expression
beats: SAY: Watch twice. Notice my eyes.
PERFORM the opening head down from a full page, then with one card, looking up.
ASK: Which version had you listening? 1 or 2?
5 sec. Cue: Fingers at your chest... show me.
EXPECT: 2
ASK: What changed when I used the card?
15 sec. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: you looked at us; more expression
SAY: A full page makes you read. A card lets you speak.
trap: thinking cue cards mean memorising every word.
Fix: say the card holds key words; you know the rest.
notes.prep: Low-entry launch. Hold a full page and one index card. 3 minutes.

slides.meaning: A small card with key words to jog your memory.
slides.example: My cue card says HAND - SLIDE - OUCH.

notes.answer: a small card with key words to jog your memory
beats: POINT to the word. SAY: Cue card. Say it with me. Cue card.
SAY: A small card with key words to jog your memory.
SAY: My cue card says HAND - SLIDE - OUCH.
ASK: Why not write your whole speech on the cue card?
10 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: you'd read it, not say it; no eye contact
trap: Fix: say if you can read it aloud word for word, it's too long.
notes.prep: Cue card is today's delivery tool.

slides.title: My big finish, then my cards

rows: So, our school needs ten shade trees.
Next summer, touch the slide. No ouch.
Say yes at Tuesday's council meeting.

notes.answer: restate, echo the hook, call to action; key words on the card
beats: POINT to Echo the hook.
SAY: My speech started with ouch. It ends with no ouch.
Full circle. They feel it close.
POINT to Call to action.
SAY: One action. A day. They know exactly what to do.
POINT to My cue card.
SAY: Only the words that jog my memory. Three or four. Capitals.
ASK: What goes on a cue card, sentences or key words?
5 sec. Cue: Everyone, together, on three.
EXPECT: key words
trap: ending with thank you for listening as the last strong line.
Fix: say the action is the last strong line; thank you comes after.
notes.stretch: Mark one pause and one stressed word.
notes.help: Use the frame: So... Please... Thank you.
notes.prep: Model finish and cards. Critical feature: key words, not sentences.

slides.title: Name the part
slides.pivot: ask does it repeat, look back, or ask?
slides.followUp: cold call one student: how do you know?

items.text: So, polar bears need us to act now.
Remember that magpie? Let's make sure it's the last.
Sign the petition at the office by Friday.
Imagine that playground again. Now add trees.
Switch off at the wall tonight. Every night.

say: One finger: restate. Two: echo the hook. Three: call to action.
trap: calling every strong line a call to action.
Fix: ask does it tell us to do something?
notes.stretch: Write the missing two parts for one item.
notes.help: Look for a doing word at the start.

options.text: Imagine a 41 degree slide. That's our yard, and we need shade now.
options.misconception: a full sentence; you will read it
too little; nothing to jog the memory

beats: SAY: Three cue cards for the same opening.
ASK: Which cue card is best?
10 sec. Cue: voices off, everyone points to A, B or C.
EXPECT: pointing to B
SCAN the room, back row first.
80%+ -> reveal, cold call: say the opening from card B.
Less -> try speaking from each card, re-ask.
REVEAL after pointing is scanned.
SAY: B. Enough to remember, too little to read.
trap: pointing to A because it's safest.
Fix: ask where will your eyes be with card A?
notes.prep: Decision point before carding. Under 80% means one more shrink done together.

slides.title: Shrink it
slides.pivot: circle the nouns and numbers, then keep three
slides.followUp: cold call one board: say the sentence from your key words

items.text: Every minute, a garbage truck of plastic enters the ocean.
Malala said one child, one teacher, one book and one pen can change the world.
Walking to school saves petrol and wakes up your brain.

say: Three or four key words only. Capitals.
trap: keeping little words like the and of.
Fix: student crosses out every word they'd remember anyway.
notes.stretch: Say the full sentence from your key words.
notes.help: Circle the numbers and naming words first.

slides.title: Finish and card it
slides.task: Work through your Worksheet. Finish your conclusion, make five cue cards on index cards, then time your whole speech with a partner.

notes.answer: a conclusion with restate, hook echo and action, plus key-word cards
beats: POINT to the task.
SAY: Your finish, then five cue cards. Then time it.
SAY: Read the task, complete each part, check your work.
Finished? Extension next. Everyone, together, on three.
CIRCULATE. Ask: read me card 3.
Could you read it word for word? Then shrink it.
ASK: Give your speech from your cards. Partner times you.
120 sec each. Turn and tell, partner A first.
EXPECT: close to 2 minutes
trap: a speech under one minute because it was rushed.
Fix: student adds the pauses they marked.
notes.stretch: Extension: mark pauses and stress, then plan for a tough question.
notes.help: Supported Worksheet: picture-clue choices, a card done, a frame.
notes.prep: Independent finishing and carding; Week 9 is rehearse and deliver. SC2.

slides.extendedTask: a worksheet ending in the student's conclusion and five key-word cue cards

slides.title: Show what you know
questions: Bikes are cheaper than cars, keep you fit, and never get stuck in traffic.
Write the key words for a cue card.

notes.answer: e.g. BIKES - CHEAP - FIT - NO TRAFFIC
beats: SAY: A new sentence. Card it.
ASK: Write three or four key words.
30 sec. Cue: Write it... Chin it... Show me.
EXPECT: CHEAP, FIT, TRAFFIC
RECORD who writes the full sentence. Check their cards first in Week 9.
trap: Fix: none now, record the name.
notes.prep: Exit evidence for SC2 on a new sentence. One board per student.

slides.reflectionPrompt: What is the very last thing your audience will hear you say?

beats: SAY: Let's read our I can lines together. Everyone, together, on three.
ASK: How ready is your speech for rehearsal next week?
5 sec. Cue: Thumbs only, voices off. Show me... now.
EXPECT: thumbs up, sideways or down
RECORD each thumb down beside the exit boards.
ASK: What is the very last thing your audience will hear you say?
20 sec. Turn and tell, partner B first.
EXPECT: the call to action
notes.prep: Cards and speech stay in the folder for Week 9. SC2.
